cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved wooden Edo altar of the hand (ikegobo), a well-known Benin/Edo ritual object with high-relief figures and interlace patterning matching the description exactly. It is ritual sculpture rather than a building, so architectural is the wrong category, but the object clearly belongs to Edo tradition.

physical.title: altar
physical.summary: Altar of the Hand (ikegobo); made of wood. Cylindrical in form with figures in high relief around outside. Central figure of male figure wearing cap, necklace and skirt. Holds eben sword aloft in right hand, left hand supported by attendant holding shield and spears in left hand. Similar attendant on other side of central figure. Padlocked boxes flank central figure. Images of hands, kola nuts and leaves depicted around back of altar. Band of interalce patterning around base. Top surface of altar has two mudfish depicted in low relief surrounded by interlace and geometric patterns. Short projection towards back edge of top surface.
